---
title: "Pre-push checks"
description: "Run the build-free changed-files gate before pushing so cheap CI failures are caught locally in seconds."
updatedAt: "2026-11-17"
audience: developers
---

## Why this gate exists

Most avoidable CI failures come from cheap checks skipped before pushing: Oxc
formatting, `flutter analyze` infos (fatal in CI), TypeScript errors such as
`TS6059` (a package importing app source outside its `rootDir`), stale generated
inventories and branch names the checker rejects. `bun validate` is too heavy for
agent machines because its Turbo graph can build workspace dependencies, so it
is not run locally. `bun check:changed` is the replacement before every push.

```bash
bun check:changed                 # working tree vs merge base with origin/main
bun check:changed --dry-run       # print the planned steps only
bun check:changed --only oxc    # one step (ids or prefixes such as type-check)
bun check:changed --skip vitest   # skip a step family
bun check:changed --committed     # committed changes only (the hook's mode)
bun check:changed --files a.ts b.ts
```

It never runs builds or `bun validate`. Turbo is used only as
`turbo run type-check test --dry=json --filter=...[merge-base]` to choose
packages. That dry run does not execute tasks, including any task whose
`dependsOn` includes a build. If the dry command fails, selection falls back to
transitive reverse dependents. Small repository scripts run directly;
Vitest, type-check and `flutter analyze` are queued through `ttr resources run`
when resource control is installed and enabled (`--no-ttr` opts out). Without
the `~/.bun/bin/ttr` directory entry, the gate warns and runs sequentially with Vitest
capped at two workers. An invalid installed global CLI or unsafe ancestor bin
alias still fails closed; a workspace binary is never used as a fallback. A dangling global launcher symlink or missing package bin target is a broken installation, not an absent CLI: reinstall with `bun add -g tuturuuu` before retrying.

`ttr check` runs this same gate with `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2`, `TURBO_CONCURRENCY=2`,
and the gate's `node --test --test-concurrency=2`. It refuses hostname
`Mac-Mini-M4` and host id `m4` with exit 2 and does not start the check.
Remote Turbo cache is used only when `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM` are already
set in the environment.

## What runs for which paths

| Changed paths                                                                           | Steps                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Any                                                                                     | Branch name (same pattern as `branch-name-check.yaml`), source-size ceiling, docs inventory and app SEO `--check`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| JS/TS/JSON/CSS outside `apps/mobile`                                                    | Oxfmt `--check` (0.74.0) and blocking Oxlint `--deny-warnings` (1.89.0)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `packages/internal-api/**`, `packages/sdk/**`, `packages/utils/**`, `packages/types/**` | SDK portable source approval (`sdk-portable`): resolves the source closure and checks its allowlist without emitting files or running TypeScript. Utils and types are conservatively scoped to cover portable imports.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `apps/*` or `packages/*` source                                                         | App-session, satellite cookie and server-console guards                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A workspace's source, `tsconfig*.json` or `package.json`                                | Type-check with `tsc --noEmit` of the dry-graph packages (changed packages and dependents). A failed dry graph uses reverse dependents instead. The gate does not run the Turbo `type-check` task, because that task depends on `^build`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A workspace's related tests                                                             | Changed and colocated tests use `node --test --test-concurrency=2` when they import `node:test` or their package's `test` script uses `node --test`; explicit Vitest imports retain Vitest; files that import `bun:test` run with `bun test` from their workspace directory (the Meet realtime Durable Object suites, which Node cannot load). Vitest steps run `vitest related` on the changed source files with `--maxWorkers=2`. Each test file runs under one runner. Oxfmt and Oxlint stay on the changed files. |
| `scripts/`, `.github/actions/`, `plugins/`                                              | Changed and sibling `node --test` files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/`                                              | Workflow concurrency (including the main validation inventory), Bun pin, workflow-config and `pr-label-gate` policy tests                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `apps/mobile/`                                                                          | `flutter gen-l10n` first when ARB files changed, `dart format` on changed Dart files, then `flutter analyze lib test` exactly as `mobile.yaml` runs it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `apps/*/messages/*.json`                                                                | i18n sort and en/vi key parity                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Migrations, docs, web API routes                                                        | Migration timestamps, docs audit, legacy route wrappers, mobile API mappings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Migrations, the public-schema allowlist, generated types, mobile/Discord or app/package source| [Public schema guard](/build/devops/public-schema-privatization#guard-no-new-public-relations) (`bun db:public-guard`)

Oxfmt and Oxlint both block pushes on failures. The root Oxc configs define the
active scope and explicit rule exclusions; exact-commit CI remains required.

In hook mode, every non-deletion `refs/heads/*` destination from Git's pre-push
stdin is validated, including additional branches whose commits differ from
HEAD. Tracking cannot override an invalid destination such as `tmp/agent`.
Branch deletions and tag names do not undergo branch-name validation.

Without push refs, local `tmp/` branches with a configured tracking branch validate that tracked
branch name and print both names. Untracked `tmp/` branches still fail, and other
local branch names always validate themselves. This keeps the check blocking
while allowing temporary agent worktrees that track a valid publication branch.
The manual label `branch name fix/routing (tracking for tmp/agent)` validates only
the configured upstream name, which may name a local or remote branch. It does
not certify a future push destination. For example, `git push origin tmp/agent`
is still rejected by the opted-in hook even when the upstream is `fix/routing`.
CI continues to validate the actual published branch name.

Ancestor bin refusals can be caused by stale links in the main checkout even
when the current worktree is healthy. `--no-ttr` does not bypass that safety
check. Inspect the listed ancestor's manifest and links: refresh declared
workspace dependencies with `~/.bun/bin/ttr resources run -- bun install --force`,
keeping legitimate package links. Remove links only after proving they are
undeclared orphan symlinks; follow the conditional
[orphan alias recovery procedure](/reference/packages/sdk#orphan-workspace-aliases).

For Vite/Oxc validation, keep the worktree container outside another checkout.
An enclosing checkout's TypeScript project references can cause `TSCONFIG_ERROR`
for a missing config package even when the worktree's own package links resolve.
Move only the owned worktree with `git worktree move`, retain TTR admission, and
rerun the failed contract; do not change compiler settings to hide this failure.

## Type-checking without built declarations

CI builds `@tuturuuu/types`, `supabase`, `internal-api` and `masonry` before
type-checking. Local checkouts usually lack those `dist` declarations, which
produces thousands of missing-module errors and implicit-`any` cascades. The
gate runs `-p <project> --noEmit --incremental false --composite false` per
project and classifies diagnostics:

- With every workspace declaration present, all diagnostics block.
- When declarations are cold, missing-module errors citing an unbuilt workspace
  package are ignored. Configuration errors (`TS5xxx`/`TS6xxx`, including
  `TS6059`) and errors in changed files that do not import an unbuilt package
  block. A changed file importing a missing package still blocks on real type
  errors such as TS2322; only implicit-any follow-ons (7005/7006/7031/7034)
  in that file are advisory. Diagnostics in unchanged files remain advisory.
- Unknown-value errors (`TS18046`) in a changed file with a confirmed missing
  workspace import appear separately as environment-gap candidates, with the
  same-file missing-import diagnostic as evidence. They remain blocking:
  diagnostic text cannot prove whether the unknown value depends on that import.
  Build the missing workspace declarations on an admitted validation host and
  rerun the gate to distinguish a cascade from a real type error. Unrelated
  unknown values in the same file retain their diagnostics and blocking status.

Shared-package changes select affected packages from the Turbo dry graph.
When that command fails, the gate keeps transitive reverse dependents from
workspace manifests. `type-check:slice` is a build-free cached Turbo task with
empty `dependsOn` and declared `*.tsbuildinfo` outputs. The gate does not
execute it: packages keep their existing `type-check` script, and running the
Turbo `type-check` task would build dependencies. Root/shared configuration changes (`package.json`, `bun.lock`, root
`tsconfig.json`, `.oxfmtrc.json` and `.oxlintrc.json`, `turbo.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `.npmrc`,
root `vitest.config.ts`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.json`, and
`packages/typescript-config`)
print **not covered; CI only** because this focused gate cannot prove their full
repository effect. CI type-checking remains authoritative.

### Optional tsrs shadow

`--checker auto` and `--checker tsc` use tsc only. Existing clean-source
qualification does not establish that tsrs catches seeded errors, so a tsrs
pass cannot replace tsc. `--checker tsrs` requests advisory comparisons, always
followed by tsc regardless of success, failure or crash. Only tsc can block.
The resolver runs only if at least one planned project is in the recorded
qualification set; unqualified-only plans fall back to tsc. Hook mode uses only
an existing `TSRS_BIN`, with no network fetch. Outside hooks, pinned npm
resolution disables install lifecycle scripts. See the
[qualification limits](/build/development-tools/tsrs-shadow-type-check).

## Worktrees nested inside another checkout

Oxc's tsconfig discovery walks upward past tsconfig files that do not include a
file, and most workspaces exclude their tests. In a standalone checkout the walk
finds nothing and the transform uses defaults, as in CI. In a worktree under
another checkout's `.worktrees/`, the walk reaches that checkout's root
`tsconfig.json`; without its `node_modules`, its package configs cannot resolve
`@tuturuuu/typescript-config` and tests fail with `TSCONFIG_ERROR`. When the gate
detects a `tsconfig.json` above the repository root, each `vitest related` step
runs through a temporary `.check-changed.vitest.config.mjs` wrapper that pins
the workspace `tsconfig.json`, then removes it. Web tests pin
`apps/web/tsconfig.json` in their own config for direct runs.

## Optional pre-push hook

`bun install` already points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The pre-push hook
is inert until you opt in:

```bash
git config tuturuuu.prePush true   # every push in this clone and its worktrees
TUTURUUU_PRE_PUSH=1 git push       # a single push
TUTURUUU_PRE_PUSH=0 git push       # skip once while opted in
```

The hook refuses tracked staged or unstaged edits so it can check the exact
pushed HEAD. It also refuses untracked files in changed workspaces and selected
reverse dependents because those files can affect type-checking and test discovery.
When script tests are selected, the fence covers `scripts/`, `plugins/` and
`.github/actions/` as well as the tests' own parent directories, so nested tests
cannot depend on untracked helpers in a parent or sibling directory.
Ignored files are excluded from this check. NUL-delimited Git paths preserve
whitespace; only option-like repository/workspace-relative prefixes are rejected
before file tools run. Internal dash directories, including Git app routes, are valid. The hook checks committed changes only and skips deletions or pushes of refs
other than `HEAD`. Agents should run `bun check:changed` explicitly before
pushing whether or not the hook is enabled.

Chain the push on the gate's own exit status: `bun check:changed && git push`.
A pipe such as `bun check:changed | tail` reports the last command's status, so
a refused or failed gate (for example a disk admission refusal) would still let
the push run. Write the output to a file and check the status instead. After a
rebase, re-run the gate on the rebased commit before pushing.

### Bun upgrade and lock normalization

Until the Bun 1.4.4 upgrade in #6427 lands, a normal `bun install` with installed
Bun 1.4.4 can normalize the 1.4.3-era `bun.lock`. The resulting tracked change
makes the opted-in hook refuse a push. Prefer `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
for the existing lock or the repository-pinned Bun version; do not commit
incidental normalization into an unrelated PR. If drift already exists, preserve
its provenance and use a clean isolated checkout. #6427 owns the normalized lock;
a passing frozen install alone does not prove a normal install leaves it stable.

## Regression coverage

`scripts/check-changed.test.js`, `scripts/check-changed/plan.test.js`,
`scripts/check-changed/type-check.test.js`, `scripts/check-changed/tsrs.test.js`
and `scripts/ts-diagnostics.test.js` cover path mapping, the branch pattern's parity with the workflow, hook opt-in,
ttr queueing, cold-declaration classification and tsc confirmation of tsrs
failures.
`scripts/check-changed/environment-gap.test.js` verifies that same-file unknown
values retain blocking status, including an unrelated value beside a missing
import, and that the report separates unverified environment-gap candidates.

Related native `node:test` files, including database script `.test.mjs` siblings, run through `node --test` even in packages whose default is Vitest. The classifier parses actual runtime imports, including CommonJS `require` and dynamic imports. Fixture strings, template text, comments, regular expressions and type-only imports cannot choose a runner. An explicit runtime Vitest import still takes precedence when a file also imports Node test helpers. Without a runner import, the owning package test script supplies the existing fallback. This runner partition avoids false “No test suite found” failures. `scripts/check-changed-runners.test.js` covers the SDK portable-build fixture and both runner directions.

### Keep host configuration types out of app programs

Mail, Calendar and Meet check Vite/Void configuration in a separate
`tsconfig.config.json` through their normal `type-check` command. Their app
programs retain runtime and test files. This prevents host tooling such as
`unplugin` from loading Bun globals into browser app types, where Bun's
`fetch.preconnect` would incorrectly become mandatory for fetch fixtures and
ordinary request wrappers. Keep the configuration check in the package gate
when moving config roots. `scripts/ci/vite-config-type-boundary.test.js` verifies
the compiler's resolved app/config roots and the package command wiring.

## Web browser and fixture test discovery

Playwright's authenticated project collects only `*.spec.ts`; its setup project
owns `auth.setup.ts`. Keep Vitest fixture tests out of browser collection.
Check discovery without starting services with
`bun run --cwd apps/web test:e2e -- --list` and require a nonzero test count.
The root Vitest project `web-e2e-fixtures` runs the employee fixture unit tests:
`bun x vitest run --project web-e2e-fixtures --maxWorkers=1`.
The chat bridge fixture remains an explicit SQL qualification target requiring
its envelope; it is not an ordinary unit test.

## Web API route inventories

`node scripts/check-mobile-api-mappings.js` checks client paths against canonical
API owners. A CLI client whose handler is not enabled can reserve an exact path
in `scripts/cli-api-route-ownership.json`, naming its owning active app and client
source. Reservations do not establish deployed handlers, authorize runtime
activation, cover child paths, or satisfy mobile route ownership. Remove the
reservation when the handler supplies ownership directly.

Moving a retained handler into `apps/web/src/app/api` changes its source digest
and import graph even when the endpoint URL stays the same. Refresh each owning
inventory after the final handler edit:

```bash
node scripts/generate-web-api-route-wrappers.js --write
node scripts/generate-docs-inventory.js
bun run --cwd apps/api generate
bun apps/web/cloudflare/generate-inventory.ts
```

Run the corresponding `--check` commands before publishing. The standalone API
uses `bun run --cwd apps/api registry:check`. The build-free changed-files gate
checks wrappers and docs inventory; it does not cover the standalone API registry
or Web Start census. Run these two checks explicitly for Web API route changes.
Generated inventories locate retained handlers; they do not establish Worker
runtime acceptance or authorize a cutover.
